title: SPA/936/2017 of State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS Vs Mukesh Kumar

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 936 of 2017
With
Delay Condonation Application No. 14523 of 2017
State of Uttarakhand and others .......... Appellants

Versus
Mukesh Kumar .......... Respondent
Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand/appellants.
Mr. Kurban Ali, Advocate for the respondent.
Dated : 22nd November, 2017

Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
 There is delay of 147 days in filing this appeal. After hearing learned
counsel for the parties, we are inclined to condone the delay. Accordingly,
the delay of 147 days in filing this appeal will stand condoned and the delay
condonation application will stand allowed.
2. Appellants are the respondents. Appellants call in question the
judgment passed by the learned Single Judge. The same reads as follows:
 "Mr. Kurban Ali, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. Vikas Pandey, Brief Holder for the State.
 Heard.
Petitioner participated in the selection process for
the post of Primary Teachers. According to the
advertisement dated 01.02.2014, the selection and
allocation of districts were to be made on the basis of
over all merit of the candidates. The petitioner gave his
option for District Udham Singh Nagar. However, the
respondents without taking into consideration the merit
determined at the time of selection have allocated
District Almora to the petitioner.
It has come on record that the persons who were
lower in the merit vis-à-vis petitioner have been
allocated stations of their choice. The respondents

2
should have considered the merit at the time of
allocating the districts.
It has also come on record that the principle of
reservation was not followed at the time of allocation of
districts.
Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. The
respondents are directed to allocate District Udham
Singh Nagar to the petitioner, within a period of six
weeks from today."
3. We notice, in fact, from the order sheet that the writ petition came to
be decided on the same day as it came before the learned Single Judge for
the first time. No counter affidavit was called for and, therefore, the
appellants did not file the counter affidavit.
4. No doubt, Mr. Kurban Ali, learned counsel for the writ petitioner
would submit that a similar matter has been disposed of and that the matter
is squarely covered. According to Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned Brief
Holder, there are contentions, which need to be considered.
5. In such circumstances, without expressing any view regarding the
merits of the matter, we are of the view that the judgment passed by the
learned Single Judge should be set aside and the writ petition may be
remitted back so that the matter is reconsidered after giving an opportunity
to file counter affidavit and exchange the pleadings.
6. In such circumstances, we allow the appeal; set aside the judgment of
the learned Single Judge and remit the matter back. We further direct that
the appellants will file their counter affidavit within a period of two weeks
from today. The case will stand listed on 13.12.2017. The respondent/writ
petitioner may also file rejoinder affidavit in the meantime. We request the
learned Single Judge to dispose of the matter at the earliest.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 22.11.2017 22.11.2017
Rahul
